Balanced statement with cautious optimism, but July 2024 SLOOS tilts the read more neutral. Banks reported broadly tight or tighter standards and weaker demand across key categories:
- C&I: Standards remained tight or tightened on net; demand softer; wider spreads and higher minimum credit scores.
- CRE: Further tightening, especially for office; weak demand and collateral concerns.
- RRE: Tighter standards across most mortgage categories; subdued demand.
- Consumer (credit card/auto/other): Continued tightening, higher required scores, larger spreads; demand softened; rising delinquency/credit quality concerns.
Many banks cited a weaker economic outlook, deteriorating collateral values, and reduced risk tolerance, with some expecting further tightening through 2024. These credit headwinds, alongside continued QT and a high-for-long policy rate, temper the headline’s “better balance” message and argue for cautiousness about growth and the pace of future easing. Net tone: slightly positive but closer to neutral than before.
